answer: The economy resists sybils by drawing grader quorums randomly from a relic registry of established identities, each of which staked reputation earned through past work. New entrants cannot bridge directly into grading duty; they must first accrue standing via verified contributions. Attackers who flood fake identities gain no voting weight because quorum sampling ignores unproven accounts, so each ripple of forged personas costs the attacker identity creation and stake without any influence, while slashing punishes collusion among sampled graders.
